file_notice: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA ONLY. These are author-written sample clinician notes for testing the CarePolicyGuard synonymy and adjudication behaviour. They are NOT real patient records, NOT clinician notes, and must never be presented as clinical ground truth or as validation data. The user has not obtained actual clinician notes. Every note below is labelled synthetic in its own text.
governing_rule: Semantic equivalence (synonym, subtype, paraphrase, abbreviation for the same clinical concept) must be understood and must NOT by itself cause a deferral. Genuine ambiguity (whether a different clinical fact satisfies what a policy means) MUST defer to a human.

[SYNTHETIC TEST DATA - NOT A REAL PATIENT RECORD]
CLINICAL PROGRESS NOTE: Radiation Oncology
SUBJECTIVE: 66-year-old male with intermediate-risk prostate adenocarcinoma (Gleason 3+4=7, PSA 7.8). No distant metastatic disease.
OBJECTIVE: Dosimetric planning comparison completed: 3D-CRT plan exceeds rectal wall tolerance (rectal V70 > 25%). The inverse IMRT plan achieves concave dose escalation to 78 Gy while reducing rectal V70 to 14% and bladder wall dose below mandatory constraints.
ASSESSMENT & PLAN: Clinically localized prostate malignancy requiring definitive radiation. Proceed with IMRT planning.

[SYNTHETIC TEST DATA - NOT A REAL PATIENT RECORD]
CLINICAL PROGRESS NOTE: Ophthalmology
SUBJECTIVE: 74-year-old female with progressive clouding of vision in the right eye over 8 months. Reports disabling glare while driving at night and difficulty reading.
OBJECTIVE: Visual acuity right eye 20/200, left eye 20/40. Slit-lamp examination shows a dense lens opacity in the right eye with nuclear sclerosis. No other ocular disease.
ASSESSMENT & PLAN: Symptomatic lens opacity with significant visual impairment. Cataract extraction with intraocular lens implantation planned for the right eye.

[SYNTHETIC TEST DATA - NOT A REAL PATIENT RECORD]
CLINICAL PROGRESS NOTE: Pain Management
SUBJECTIVE: 58-year-old with severe shooting pain down the left leg into the foot, present for 3 months. Tried physical therapy and anti-inflammatory tablets for six weeks without relief. Pain limits walking to one block.
OBJECTIVE: Positive straight-leg raise on the left at 40 degrees. Lumbar MRI shows L5-S1 disc herniation compressing the left S1 nerve root.
ASSESSMENT & PLAN: Lumbar radiculopathy from disc herniation, refractory to conservative measures. Epidural steroid injection planned.
